d.g: denoting a quantity consisting of one more than eight and one less than ten
the cardinal number that is the sum of eight and one
Any of the genus Ixia of cormous plants native to South Africa.
Any of various ticks of the family Ixodidae.
Nothing; nix; often in the phrase "ixnay on ...", indicating something that must not be mentioned, often in Pig Latin
d.x: Ixnay on the "W-A-L-K" while the dogs can hear you.

d.g: To reject or cancel something; nix.
d.x: If I wasn't so bored out of my mind, I would have ixnayed that idea.

ixnay.e: Pig Latin version of nix; possibly the only Pig Latin word to enter common American English besides amscray and igpay. Ixnay and amscray were used widely in The Three Stooges shorts and The Flintstones episodes, possibly the main sources of popularity for the words.

d.g: Any of the flowering plants in the genus Ixora.
d.x: He could see[…]some ragged red ixora hedges that need fixing up.

ixora.e: Borrowed from translingual Ixora, from Sanskrit ई॒श्व॒र (īśvará).

d.g: A municipality whose municipal seat is the city of the same name.

Ixmiquilpan.e: Borrowed from Spanish Ixmiquilpan, from a Nahuan language, equivalent to Classical Nahuatl Itzmiquilpan, from itzmīquilitl (“purslane”) + -pan (locative suffix), calqued from Mezquital Otomi Nts’u̱tk’ani, from tsꞌu̱tkꞌǎni (“purslane”).

d.g: A municipality of Oaxaca whose municipal seat is the town of the same name.

Ixcuintepec.e: Borrowed from Spanish Ixcuintepec, from a Nahuan language (equivalent to Classical Nahuatl Itzcuintepēc, from itzcuintli (“dog”) + tepētl (“mountain”) + -c (locative suffix)), calqued from a Mixe language (e.g. Totontepec Mixe Oc Cuvajcm, from oc (“dog”) + cuvajc (“head”)).
